claims.text: In situ high-temperature STEM combined with EDS can reveal mechanistic aspects of oxidation in Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 HEA.
In situ STEM-EDS can track elemental redistribution within nanoprecipitates during oxidation.
The initial material is an additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 HEA containing dual nanoprecipitates.
The alloy can be exposed to a controlled high-temperature oxidizing environment during in situ STEM-EDS analysis.
Temperatures of 700–900°C are representative of the contemplated high-temperature oxidation conditions.
In situ monitoring can capture oxidation-induced changes in real time.
Nanoprecipitates can act as reservoirs for oxidation-prone elements.
Nanoprecipitates can serve as sites for elemental segregation during oxidation.
Selective oxidation of elements within nanoprecipitates causes elemental redistribution.
Elemental redistribution within nanoprecipitates may initiate or modify oxide-scale formation.
Capturing elemental redistribution with STEM-EDS can elucidate the relationship between nanoprecipitate chemistry and overall oxidation behavior.
Real-time STEM-EDS will show changes in the elemental composition of nanoprecipitates during oxidation.
Enrichment or depletion of specific alloying elements will occur concomitantly with oxide-layer development.
Room-temperature STEM-EDS mapping can establish the initial elemental distribution and microstructural baseline.
The sensitivity and spatial resolution of in situ STEM-EDS may be insufficient to capture rapid or subtle elemental changes within nanoprecipitates.
